summary: A timeline article published after Jada Pinkett Smith revealed in a People interview that she and Will Smith have been separated for seven years, though they remain married and are "still figuring it out." It traces their relationship from meeting on The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air in 1994 through marriage, children, rumours, August Alsina's affair claims, Will's memoir and the 2022 Oscars slap.
one_line: Timeline of Will Smith and Jada Pinkett Smith's relationship from 1994 to 2022, following her October 2023 revelation of a seven-year separation.
key_facts: Jada Pinkett Smith revealed in a People interview published 11 October 2023 that she and Will Smith had been separated for seven years; she said they are "still figuring it out."
Jada said they had been separated for six years at the time of the 2022 Academy Awards, when Will slapped Chris Rock.
Will and Jada have been married since 1997 and have son Jaden, 25, and daughter Willow, 22; Will also has son Trey, 30, with first wife Sheree Zampino.
Jada met Will in 1994 after auditioning for the role of his girlfriend on The Fresh Prince of Bel-Air; she did not get the part, and Will was still married to Zampino.
Will and Jada began seriously dating in 1995 after he finalised his divorce from Zampino.
Will proposed in November 1997 and they married one month later in Baltimore; Jada told People in 2019 she never wanted to get married but her mother and Will pushed for it.
In 2013 Jada wrote on Facebook that she and Will can do whatever they want because they trust each other, adding "this means we have a GROWN one" rather than an open relationship.
In 2015 Will wrote on Facebook that he and Jada were "NOT GETTING A DIVORCE."
In 2018 on TIDAL's Rap Radar podcast, Will said they call themselves "life partners" with "no deal breakers."

In 2020 August Alsina claimed he had dated Jada while she was married and that Will gave his "blessing"; Jada's reps first denied it, then she confirmed on Red Table Talk that she had a relationship with him while she and Will were separated.
Will's memoir, released in November 2021, said the structure of their life was "strangling both of us" though neither wanted a divorce.
On CBS Sunday Morning in 2023 Will said there has never been infidelity in their marriage.
In March 2022 at the 94th Oscars Will slapped Chris Rock after Rock's "GI Jane 2" joke about Jada's shaved head, and Will then won Best Actor.
